summary: Partial author continuation for issue #69 by ChatGPT Pro — cgp-aa0b3d0309fb. Four links (one incoming explicit, three outgoing inferred) and one Gaussian affine-law rescope overlap remain. Pinned source inspection corrects determinacy to a finite-measure theorem and resolves the existing uniform-law normalization through ProbabilityTheory.cond. The cumulative 218 identifiers comprise the original 212-roadmap snapshot, including the now-retired FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration, plus six new definitions. Fresh campaign summary and new-root-document screens are distinguished from inherited upstream reading and full candidate-stage reads. Catalogue-wide full-text closure is still unfinished; see the handoff. The official validator passed on the previous PR #786 head, not yet on this revised packet.

Attach this reuse to the Layer-1 uniqueness applications, not to every moment calculation. The pinned Tau Ceti implementation supplies TauCeti.Measure.ext_of_forall_integral_pow_eq and its exists_integrable_exp variant for two finite measures on R: every polynomial moment agrees and BOTH measures have 0 in the interior of their exponential-integrability sets, or each has some integrable exp(a*abs(x)) with a>0. No density or absolute-continuity hypothesis is needed. The source was read at f790474821cf4256814db967cb154e7af3d0c369 in TauCeti/Probability/Moments/Determinacy.lean; this is existing-library reuse, not a claim that B1 must be rebuilt. links.reason: The nonzero-scale Cauchy non-integrability theorem supplies OptimalTransport Layer 3 item 2's concrete counterexample. For the probability law mu=cauchyMeasure x0 gamma with gamma nonzero, a finite second moment would imply integrability of id by L2-to-L1 inclusion, a contradiction. A constant-shift inequality handles moments about any basepoint. The separate assertion W2(mu,mu)=0 uses the diagonal coupling in OptimalTransport and needs no finite moment. Exclude gamma=0, whose Dirac law lies in P2. Non-integrability is an actual conclusion, not an inference from a totalized Lean integral value.

overlaps.detail: StandardDistributions Layer 5 item 3 constructs Gaussian affine pushforwards with covariance L*S*transpose(L), while OptimalTransport Layer 5 item 3 also asks to build Gaussian covariance-pushforward lemmas. This duplicates an elementary law identity, not the full statistical and transport theories. StandardDistributions permits rectangular L and positive-semidefinite S. OptimalTransport additionally needs positive-definite square-root, inverse and geometric-mean identities and their transport applications.
overlaps.proposal: Keep the elementary affine-law and covariance-pushforward theorem in StandardDistributions Layer 5, on finite real Euclidean carriers with rectangular L and S.PosSemidef. Replace the duplicate law-building clause in OptimalTransport Layer 5 item 3 with an explicit import and carrier adapter. Keep the Brenier matrix, W2 formula, interpolation, barycenters and their positive-matrix identities in OptimalTransport; keep Cholesky, Wishart densities and conditional-Gaussian laws in StandardDistributions. Do not impose positive definiteness on the affine-law theorem or extend it to arbitrary totalized covariance parameters. Emit no edge for this pair until the ownership decision is accepted. Later transport examples use their local geometry/flow interfaces, not fresh whole-roadmap reverse dependencies.
